knowledge:
- key_parameters: classes=number of classes/clusters to simulate ;; samples=number of samples to simulate ;; features=number of features to simulate ;; data=the input gene expression dataframe (e.g., toy_genes) ;; method.upper.k=the upper limit of clusters (k) to be investigated ;; number.of.comparisons=number of internal comparisons per clustering approach (higher values increase robustness and run times) ;; algorithm.1/algorithm.2=clustering algorithms to compare (e.g., "spectral", "kmeans") ;; measure.1/measure.2=distance or kernel measures associated with the algorithms (e.g., "rbfdot", "Lloyd") ;; number.of.clusters/min.k/max.k=the specific number or range of clusters to evaluate ;; step=feature step size dictating the rate of feature set increase during feature selection ;; algorithm=clustering algorithm of choice ("sc" for spectral, "km" for kmeans, "hr" for hierarchical)
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: When performing exploratory unsupervised clustering on transcriptomic/gene expression data where the optimal number of clusters, clustering algorithm, and most stable feature subset are unknown.
- pitfalls: Removal or imputation of NA values is strictly required before running any of the tools. Feasibility estimations only serve as an indication of dataset fitness based on dimensions (samples, features, clusters) and do not account for the actual biological signal in the data.

workflows.name: automated_clustering_cascade
workflows.intent: Run the entire automated machine learning cascade to select features, determine the optimal number of clusters, and perform clustering on gene expression data.
input: expression_matrix.csv (a gene expression dataframe with samples as rows/columns, containing no NA values)
workflows.stages: 1. Run the automated cascade using omada ;; 2. Extract partition agreement, feature selection, cluster voting, and sample membership results ;; 3. Plot the diagnostic results
workflows.code:
omada.analysis <- omada(toy_genes, method.upper.k = 6)
pa.scores <- get_partition_agreement_scores(omada.analysis)
fs.scores <- get_feature_selection_scores(omada.analysis)
fs.optimal.features <- 
  get_feature_selection_optimal_features(omada.analysis)
fs.optimal.number.of.features <- 
  get_feature_selection_optimal_number_of_features(omada.analysis)

cv.scores <- get_cluster_voting_scores(omada.analysis)
cv.memberships <- get_cluster_voting_memberships(omada.analysis)
cv.metrics.votes <- get_cluster_voting_metric_votes(omada.analysis)
cv.k.votes <- get_cluster_voting_k_votes(omada.analysis)
sample.memberships <- get_sample_memberships(omada.analysis)

plot_partition_agreement(omada.analysis)
plot_feature_selection(omada.analysis)
plot_cluster_voting(omada.analysis)

workflows.name: modular_step_by_step_clustering
workflows.intent: Manually execute the step-by-step modular pipeline to analyze dataset feasibility, select the best clustering method, perform feature selection, vote on the optimal cluster count, and run the final optimal clustering.
input: expression_matrix.csv (a gene expression dataframe with samples as rows/columns, containing no NA values)
workflows.stages: 1. Assess dataset feasibility based on dimensions or existing data statistics using feasibilityAnalysis or feasibilityAnalysisDataBased ;; 2. Select the most appropriate clustering method using clusteringMethodSelection or compare specific algorithms using partitionAgreement ;; 3. Select the most stable feature subset using featureSelection ;; 4. Estimate the optimal number of clusters using clusterVoting ;; 5. Execute the final partitioning using optimalClustering
workflows.code:
new.dataset.analysis <- feasibilityAnalysis(classes = 4, samples = 50, 
                                            features = 15)
existing.dataset.analysis <- feasibilityAnalysisDataBased(data = toy_genes, 
                                                          classes = 3)
average.sts.k <- get_average_stabilities_per_k(new.dataset.analysis)
maximum.st <- get_max_stability(new.dataset.analysis)
average.st <- get_average_stability(new.dataset.analysis)
generated.ds <- get_generated_dataset(new.dataset.analysis)

method.results <- clusteringMethodSelection(toy_genes, method.upper.k = 3, 
                                            number.of.comparisons = 2)
pa.scores <- get_partition_agreement_scores(method.results)
plot_partition_agreement(method.results)

agreement.results <- partitionAgreement(toy_genes, algorithm.1 = "spectral", 
                                        measure.1 = "rbfdot", 
                                        algorithm.2 = "kmeans",
                                        measure.2 = "Lloyd", 
                                        number.of.clusters = 3)
pa.scores <- get_agreement_scores(agreement.results)

feature.selection.results <-  featureSelection(toy_genes, min.k = 3, max.k = 6,
                                               step = 3)
feature.selection.scores <- get_average_feature_k_stabilities(feature.selection.results)
optimal.number.of.features <- get_optimal_number_of_features
optimal.features <- get_optimal_features(feature.selection.results)
plot_average_stabilities(feature.selection.results)

cluster.voting.results <- clusterVoting(toy_genes, 4,8,"sc")
internal.metric.scores <- get_internal_metric_scores(cluster.voting.results)
cluster.memberships.k <- get_cluster_memberships_k(cluster.voting.results)
metric.votes.k <- get_metric_votes_k(cluster.voting.results)
vote.frequencies.k <- get_vote_frequencies_k(cluster.voting.results)
plot_vote_frequencies(cluster.voting.results)

sample.memberships <- optimalClustering(toy_genes, 4, "spectral")
memberships <- get_optimal_memberships(sample.memberships)
optimal.stability <- get_optimal_stability_score(sample.memberships)
optimal.parameter <- get_optimal_parameter_used(sample.memberships)
